reasons: The cited text (Section 7.7) is squarely a Customer-payable liquidated damages clause — 15% of annual Fees per week after a ten-day grace — so the deviation classification under rule LD is correct and the severity (high, arguably walk-away given weekly compounding) is well supported.

The redline deletes the entire paragraph, which is the minimal edit that reaches the preferred position ('no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer'); the clause contains nothing but the LD obligation, so no salvageable language is lost.

The comment accurately describes what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers a sensible substitute (simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts) rather than merely deleting the Vendor's remedy, matching the required tone and prefix.
Deterministic check confirms the operation applies; the high changed-character ratio is expected and justified because the rule requires removal of the whole LD obligation.
